profile.name: The Shorekeeper
profile.introduction: The Shorekeeper of the Black Shores, a mysterious divine being governing the essence of aloofness, emerges in response to your summon. Having spent eons in guardianship, the first stirrings of emotion and desire awaken within her heart, fostering a firm determination to connect with the world — and with you.
profile.review:
Shorekeeper is a 5-star Spectro Rectifier generalist Support and healer character. She shares a similar role to Verina and can similarly fit in almost any team composition. Her unique aspect is her ability to buff allies’ CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG, which usually allows her to outperform Verina in the raw damage multiplication department. Now let's dive into her kit.

Key Mechanics

Shorekeeper’s most important mechanic is her Stellarealm. It is summoned by casting her Ultimate, and is upgraded each time one of your characters casts their Intro, up to 2 times to max its effects. It lasts 30s at S0 and has the following effects on all allies within its range:

  • Outer Stellarealm (Baseline) - Coloured blue, it continuously heals all allies once every 3 seconds;

  • Inner Stellarealm (After 1 Intro) - Coloured purple, it increases CRIT Rate according to Shorekeeper’s Energy Regen (max 12.5% at 250% Energy Regen);

  • Supernal Stellarealm (After 2 Intro) - Coloured gold, it increases CRIT DMG according to Shorekeeper’s Energy Regen (max 25% at 250% Energy Regen).

These effects are intended to scale well with Hypercarry damage dealers: the max ramp-up will only be achieved once Shorekeeper and another character on the team have finished their rotations, so it’s intended for you to play Shorekeeper in a composition with another single-target buffer (Hybrid) and a main damage dealer (DPS). She isn’t limited to these types of compositions, but they definitely tend to be her best use cases.

Her other key supportive ability is her Outro, which grants the entire party a 15% Damage Amplification buff for 30 seconds. It also provides up to 5 free Perfect Dodges that you can trigger by dodging after being interrupted. 

Rotation Concepts

Since the two abilities we already detailed form the core of her kit and are the focus of her rotation, we can form a simple rotational idea:

  • Generate as much as Concerto Energy as fast as possible,

  • Summon the Stellarealm and then immediately perform her Outro triggering another character's Intro to upgrade the realm immediately and apply Shorekeeper’s Outro buff,

  • After which you only require 1 more Intro to fully upgrade the realm.

To do this, she has a few tools she can use. Notably, her Forte gauge allows her to cast a special Forte Heavy Attack that generates a good chunk of Concerto. It can be built up by using Basic Attacks. Forte can also be consumed via a Mid-Air Attack, but this tends to be slow and less commonly used.

Each Basic Attack generates 1 Forte except for the Basic Attack 3 which generates 2 and can be instantly cancelled on hit while still retaining its full damage, Forte, and Concerto generation. This is a key concept used in all of Shorekeeper’s best rotations.

Her Skill is also a great source of Concerto Energy. As long as it’s not instantly interrupted, it’ll summon some butterflies that can generate Concerto very quickly. The Forte Heavy Attack has the same effect, so to optimize rotation time, we can have the summoned butterflies hit during her Ultimate animation right before her Outro for maximum time saves.

Finally, let's talk about Shorekeeper's Intro skill, which she has two of - a standard one and an empowered one accessible only if the highest tier Stellarealm is active. The standard Intro will generally never be used as you want Shorekeeper to cast her Outro first in her rotation, and you shouldn’t switch her back in once that’s done and her Ultimate is cast, until your 2 other characters have done their full rotations. 

However, her enhanced Intro is a key component of her Concerto generation in every rotation after her first, it deals a good amount of damage as it’ll always CRIT, and it scales off her HP (like her healing does). So you’ll always want to make use of it when it’s the right time to switch back to Shorekeeper. It’s a decent burst of damage, healing, and most importantly, it gives a high amount of Concerto (20/100). In this logic, having a weapon that helps with Concerto generation, like her Signature or Variation, is particularly helpful to speed up her rotations even more.

Meta Position & Conclusion

We’ll put it as bluntly as we can: Shorekeeper is the ONLY character from the 1.x versions that managed to survive powercreep. It’s expected for Support characters to outlast DPS ones, however in the case of Shorekeeper, she is still receiving new teams to play in today. Some modern teams that feature her as the best Support you can use include Augusta, Sigrika, Jingran, and Hsin Unison. She’s also close to the best possible choices in DPS Suoming, Galbrena and Phrolova teams, and the best possible choice for a lot of the old teams in the game that didn’t belong in niches that other specialized Supports cover, like Mornye for Tune Rupture/Strain/Mono Fusion and Chisa/Suisui for Negative Status.

Those limited Supports are her main competition, while Verina is Shorekeeper’s alternative that’s really easy to come by as she’s a permanent banner character. However, Shorekeeper still pulls her own weight as one of the best limited banner pulls for most players’ accounts to this day. Sigrika is a meta powerhouse that destroys both Tower of Adversity and Whimpering Wastes, and Jingran is one of the latest DPS releases that has firepower equal to that of the rest of the current meta. And that’s with a character who’s 2 years old in his team.

In conclusion, Shorekeeper’s main drawbacks, not belonging to any specialized meta niches, having Verina as an easy alternative, and really wanting a Concerto weapon for her rotation speed to be optimized, are not that important compared to how much value she can provide to your account, provided you have teams that can build around her. Whenever a DPS character doesn’t belong in a niche explicitly covered by a specialized Support, you can rest assured Shorekeeper will be your go-to premium Support choice. Still receiving new teams in recent times, Shorekeeper is without a doubt the longest-lasting character we’ve had in the Wuthering Waves meta, and it doesn’t look like she’ll completely fade away any time soon, even as more specialized Supports for more specialized meta niches release.
profile.pros:
• Unique buffs to CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG. One of the strongest generalist Supports;

  • Fully quickswap-friendly (so long as you account for the scaling of her Intro, which isn’t a major drawback);

  • Fast rotation, accessible weapon options, and easy to invest into, following the trend of other low-damaging general Supports;

  • The only limited character from the 1.x versions that stood the test of time, and is still receiving new teams where she is best in slot to this day occasionally.
profile.cons:
• Has no unique niche that she partakes in. Shorekeeper is only ever a generalist, never a specialized Support like Mornye or Chisa, who have specific categories of characters they excel with;

  • Her CRIT Rate buff has gotten lower value with time as more characters can naturally reach 100% CRIT Rate by themselves. This and her lack of interaction with specialized mechanics means a lot of Shorekeeper’s strength is heavily at the mercy of Kuro’s kit design for future damage dealers;

  • Awkward and lengthy rotations without a Concerto weapon available.
profile.endgameStats:
Keep in mind, Shorekeeper is a Support who deals very low personal damage, meaning investing in her damage is fully skippable. Energy Regen requirements are by far the most important stat shown.

  • HP: 20000-35000+

  • DEF: 1100+

  • CRIT Rate: 20%-40%+

  • CRIT DMG: 220-280%+

  • Energy Regen: 230% (Before Echo/Passive)

    • Remember Shorekeeper’s passive and her Fallacy of No Return Echo both increase her Energy by 10%, up to 250% total. If running a different Echo, 240% Energy Regen will be required.

  • Spectro DMG Bonus: 0-30%
profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Shorekeeper is a character who has many useful mechanics and ways to play. She’s very quickswap-friendly and animation cancel-friendly and has many useful moves that can contribute to her rotations, plus her Forte has unique mechanics. Additionally, she has many different breakpoints for Concerto buildup based on her weapon’s rank. As a result of all of this, on top of being the first character to rotate in a full team where she’s included, she has many rotation options based on your specific use case for her.

Echo Timing

Always use at the end of her rotation right before Outro to ensure maximum buff uptime on your other teammates.

For each of the rotations below:

  • Opener: The first rotation you do in a fight, when Shorekeeper’s Intro isn’t available.

  • Loop: Any rotation following the opener, when an Intro is available. 

  • S: Character Sequence level.

  • R: Concerto Weapon Rank (R0: No Concerto weapon available).

The rotations below may use the Forte carry-over mechanic from Shorekeeper’s Basic 3. Shorekeeper can cast her Forte Heavy after a Basic 3 at full Forte, and conserve both Forte stacks generated from her attack, with correct timing. Some rotations may also carry over extra Forte stacks/Concerto from swapping Mid-air Attacks before Outroing.

Additional Tips & Tricks

Shorekeeper is a very Quickswap-friendly character. Her entire rotation may be performed during other characters’ rotations, so that she can Outro nearly instantly once it’s time for her to Intro back in. 

She can also swap out of her Basic 3, Skill, Forte Heavy or Mid-Air Attack. These constitute small Quickswap windows that can save time if your characters have other meaningful attacks they can perform before they Intro in. Otherwise, these windows are not really worth exploiting as those attacks don’t last that long/can be Animation Cancelled quickly.

skills.name: Origin Calculus
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 4 consecutive attacks, dealing Spectro DMG. Each hit generates 1 Collapsed Core.

Heavy Attack

Hold the Normal Attack Button to enter Unbound Form, which consumes STA continuously. While in this form, Shorekeeper will:

  • Generate a segment of Deductive Data every second.

  • Automatically collect nearby plant collectibles.

Using up all STA or actions such as casting Basic Attack will end the Unbound Form and deal Spectro DMG to the target. Each accumulated segment of Deductive Data will convert into a segment of Empirical Data and generate a Collapsed Core.

Mid-air Attack

Consume STA to perform a Plunging Attack. Each hit generates 1 Collapsed Core. Quickly Press the Normal Attack Button after the Plunging Attack to perform Basic Attack Stage 2.

Dodge Counter

Press the Normal Attack Button after a successful Dodge to attack a target, dealing Spectro DMG.

skills.name: Chaos Theory
skills.description:
Restore HP for all nearby party members and summon 5 Dim Star Butterflies, which automatically track and attack a target, dealing Spectro DMG. Follow up with Basic Attack in time to start the Basic Attack cycle from Stage 2.

Can be performed in mid-air.

skills.name: End Loop
skills.description:
Outer Stellarealm

Generate the Outer Stellarealm to restore HP for all party members within its effective range continuously. This effect can be triggered once every 3s.

Inner Stellarealm

When a party member uses Intro Skill within the Outer Stellarealm, it evolves into the Inner Stellarealm. Within the effective range of the Inner Stellarealm, for every 0.2% of Shorekeeper's Energy Regen, all party members gain 0.01% bonus Crit. Rate, up to 12.5%. Inner Stellarealm has all the effects of the Outer Stellarealm.

Supernal Stellarealm

When a party member uses Intro Skill within the Inner Stellarealm, it evolves into the Supernal Stellarealm. Within the effective range of the Supernal Stellarealm, for every 0.1% of Shorekeeper's Energy Regen, all party members gain a 0.01% increase of Crit. DMG, up to 25%.

Supernal Stellarealm has all the effects of the Inner Stellarealm.

When Supernal Stellarealm is generated, Shorekeeper's first Intro Skill triggered in its duration will be replaced with Intro Skill Discernment. This effect takes place once each time a Supernal Stellarealm is generated.

skills.name: Astral Chord
skills.description:
Flare Star Butterfly

Hitting a target with a Normal Attack generates a Collapsed Core, which transforms into a Flare Star Butterfly after 6s. Flare Star Butterflies automatically track and attack a target, dealing Spectro DMG. If there are already 5 Collapsed Cores, Shorekeeper's next Normal Attack hit will instantly convert a Collapsed Core into a Flare Star Butterfly.

Illation

When Shorekeeper has 5 segments of Empirical Data, casting Heavy Attack will consume all segments to pull in nearby targets, dealing Spectro DMG. Meanwhile, all generated Collapsed Cores will instantly transform into Flare Star Butterflies.

Transmutation

When Shorekeeper has 5 segments of Empirical Data, casting Mid-air Attack will consume all segments to deal Spectro DMG. Meanwhile, all generated Collapsed Cores will instantly transform into Flare Star Butterflies. Quickly press the Normal Attack Button afterward to perform Basic Attack Stage 2.

Empirical Data

Shorekeeper can hold up to 5 segments of Empirical Data.

  • Obtain 1 segment of Empirical Data when Basic Attack Stage 1, 2, or 4 hits a target.

  • Obtain 2 segments of Empirical Data when Basic Attack Stage 3 hits a target.

  • Obtain 1 segment of Empirical Data when Mid-air Attack hits a target.

  • Obtain 1 segment of Empirical Data when Dodge Counter hits a target.

skills.name: Life Entwined
skills.description: When a Resonator other than Shorekeeper takes a fatal blow, they will not be knocked out and will instead be healed for 50% of Shorekeeper's HP while Shorekeeper loses the same amount of HP. Shorekeeper's HP will not go below 1 from this effect. This effect can be triggered once every 10 minutes.

skills.name: Self Gravitation
skills.description: When the Resonator on the field is within the effective range of a Stellarealm, Shorekeeper's Energy Regen increases by 10%. If Rover is on the same team, Rover's Energy Regen also increases by 10%.

skills.name: Proof of Existence
skills.description:
Enlightenment

Shorekeeper appears to restore HP for all nearby party members and summon 5 Dim Star Butterflies, which automatically track and attack a target, dealing Spectro DMG. This is considered Resonance Skill DMG.

Discernment

When a Supernal Stellarealm is generated, Shorekeeper's first Intro Skill triggered in its duration will be replaced with Intro Skill Discernment. Casting Discernment ends the current Stellarealm, restores HP for all nearby party members, and deals Spectro DMG to the targets. This attack is guaranteed to be a Critical Hit dealing Resonance Liberation DMG. The Intro Skill Discernment can only be cast one time for each Supernal Stellarealm generated.

skills.name: Binary Butterfly
skills.description:
Shorekeeper summons 1 Flare Star Butterfly and 1 Dim Star Butterfly to circle the Resonator on the field for up to 30s, granting the following effects:

  • If the Resonator on the field is hit or launched, tapping the Dodge Button allows the Resonator to immediately recover from the interruption, triggering a successful Dodge. The Resonator launched in the air can land on the ground standing if they are close to the ground. This effect can be triggered up to 5 time(s).

  • All nearby party members' DMG is Amplified by 15%.

dupes.dupe1:
The Stellarealms generated by Resonance Liberation End Loop gain the following enhancements:

  • The effective range of the healing and buffs is extended by 150%

  • The duration is extended by 10s.

  • Casting Intro Skill Discernment no longer ends the existing Stellarealm.
dupes.dupe2: The Outer Stellarealm now increases the ATK of all nearby party members by 40%.
dupes.dupe3: Casting Resonance Liberation End Loop grants Shorekeeper 20 Concerto Energy. This effect can be triggered once every 25s.
dupes.dupe4: Gain 70% additional Healing Bonus when casting Resonance Skill Chaos Theory.
dupes.dupe5: Extend the ranges of the pulling effect of Basic Attack Stage 3 by 50% and Illation by 30%.
dupes.dupe6: Increase the DMG Multiplier of Intro Skill Discernment by 42%. Casting Intro Skill Discernment increases Shorekeeper's Crit. DMG by 500%.

profile.synergyNote: The Shorekeeper is very flexible and can be used as the third slot buffer for any team in the game currently. While some options outshine her in specific teams, she is the most widely usable, generally effective Support that exists and does not have any particular synergies — she’s fantastic with everyone!

weapons.Comment: Shorekeeper's Signature is her best weapon but not by a big difference compared to Variation. It does provide a 14% team-wide ATK boost when casting Shorekeeper's skill and provides an extra Concerto boost when casting Ultimate. Additionally, it increases Energy Regen by a massive amount, making reaching Shorekeeper's 230% requirement easy. However, due to providing lower amounts of Concerto than an R5 Variation, its competition is fierce as this weapon makes Shorekeeper's opening rotation noticeably slower.

The best 4-star weapon in the game for many players, Variation provides a simple, yet massive Concerto boost when casting Skill on top of a massive amount of Energy Regen. This weapon speeds up Shorekeeper's rotation significantly and makes her rotations quick and smooth, making it one of the best choices very close to her Signature even at R1.
The best option for Shorekeeper that doesn't require any gacha. Provides a big amount of Energy Regen and a small ATK% boost when casting Skill, acquired for free via crafting.

More healing-focused option for Shorekeeper which is also given for free via an Exploration quest in Rinascita. Provides the same amount of Energy Regen as the above options, but has the added pro of increasing Healing Bonus by 16% for 15s when casting Ultimate. Better than Rectifier#25 if the player desires more healing on the team, but it is not a necessity.

echoes.Comment: Offers a 10% unconditional Healing% boost and an most importantly a 15% ATK% boost for the entire team, lasting 30 seconds whenever you heal yourself or any of your allies. This bonus can be triggered by character abilities and weapon effects, is easy to keep active 100% of the time and is a big help for all party members.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Grants 10% Energy Regen on cast, making it possible to run a Spectro DMG 3-cost on Shorekeeper using 4-star weapons while still reaching the 230% Energy Regen requirement Shorekeeper must meet, which can boost her personal damage a good amount. On top of this, the Echo also grants the entire team a 10% boost to ATK for 20 seconds and deals damage based on the wearers HP, so it will slightly boost both Shorekeeper's and the whole team's damage contribution, making it her best choice generally.

echoes.Comment: Niche set for Shorekeeper in Jingran teams that don't feature a natural Shielld applier. Ran in favour of Rejuvenating Glow since this set grants a base 20% ATK permanently to all characters in the team as long as the healer can apply Healing constantly off-field, something Shorekeeper is capable of. 5% better than Rejuvenating Glow's 15% ATK and less clunky to use thanks to having a Summon Echo instead of a Transform one on Rejuvenating Glow (which would be Stonewall Bracer).
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Grants a Shield when summoned on cast, provides Jingran with a massive Fusion DMG Bonus boost if a Shielding teammate like Iuno isn't there to generate Shields without the need for this Echo.

echoStats.Comments: ER/Spectro is the end-goal for main stats to really increase Shorekeeper's damage as much as possible, however it may be difficult without Signature so always privilege reaching the Energy Regen requirement of 230%-240% (based on whether or not you have Fallacy of No Return equipped).
